abstract: <jats:p>This study presents the modelling and analysis of neutron spectra in the European demonstration fusion power plant (EU DEMO) helium-cooled pebble bed (HCPB) divertor using OpenMC. The OpenMC model was developed by converting an existing MCNP geometry model. The converted model was supplemented with material definitions, FENDL–3.2b and ENDF/B–VIII.0 nuclear data libraries, tally settings, variance reduction parameters, and a deuterium–tritium plasma neutron source. Neutron spectra were calculated for ten divertor components containing tungsten, a homogenized W-CuCrZr-H2O mixture, EUROFER, INCONEL alloy, titanium alloy and water. Statistical precision was assessed using median and flux-weighted relative uncertainties, both of which were below 10% in nine of the ten OpenMC regions. The OpenMC spectra were compared with previously calculated MCNP reference spectra. Energy groups with positive MCNP flux and an OpenMC/MCNP ratio not exceeding 20 were retained. Reference-normalized absolute spectral differences ranged from 8.36% to 17.65% in nine regions and reached 58.16% in the small water pipe. Unfiltered results are reported in the appendices. The analysis quantifies component-specific spectral differences and identifies the regions in which statistical precision limits the interpretation of individual energy groups.</jats:p>
title: OpenMC Modelling of Neutron Spectra in the EU DEMO HCPB Divertor and Comparison with Reference MCNP Results

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Discharge capillary plasma waveguides are key components for long-distance laser guiding, multi-GeV laser wakefield acceleration, and staged accelerator coupling. Their optical axis, matched spot size, and effective channel depth directly affect laser guiding quality and beam pointing stability, while in curved waveguides the geometric centerline is not necessarily the optical equilibrium trajectory. Here we extend the established laser centroid-oscillation diagnostic by adding a far-field angular measurement to the conventional near-field exit-position measurement. Combining the two measurements reduces the phase ambiguity of position-only diagnostics and gives a more constrained inversion of the centroid-oscillation phase. In a straight discharge capillary, the two measurements give consistent phases near 154 degrees, corresponding to a matched spot size of about 53.3 μm and an effective channel depth of about 1.25×10
                    <jats:sup>18</jats:sup>
                    cm
                    <jats:sup>−3</jats:sup>
                    under the selected guiding condition. The same diagnostic is applied to a curved capillary with a 1.25 m curvature radius, where the far-field response indicates a preferred nonzero relative injection offset. This combined measurement provides an
                    <jats:italic>in situ</jats:italic>
                    phase-space diagnostic for straight and curved plasma waveguides.
                  </jats:p>
title: Near- and far-field centroid-oscillation diagnostics of straight and curved discharge plasma waveguides

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Pulsed capacitively coupled plasmas (CCPs) exhibit strongly time-dependent electrical characteristics because the plasma density, sheath structure, and plasma conductivity change as a function of time within each pulse period. This makes impedance matching difficult when the driving frequency and matching-network elements are fixed. In this work, a self-consistent circuit-plasma simulation model is used to investigate frequency-tuned impedance matching for pulsed CCPs. The model couples an implicit PIC/MCC plasma kinetic simulation with an external RF circuit including a generator, matching network, and reactor stray branch. The plasma impedance is extracted from the simulated CCP voltage and current waveforms using Fourier analysis. Under fixed-frequency operation at
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>
                        
                      </jats:tex-math>
                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mrow>
                          <mml:mn>13.56</mml:mn>
                          <mml:mtext> </mml:mtext>
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mi>MHz</mml:mi>
                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:mrow>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    , the reflection coefficient magnitude remains high during the effective pulse-on phase and a pronounced reflected-power peak appears after pulse ignition. A frequency-tuned matching strategy is then developed by determining, from the time-dependent plasma impedance, the driving frequency that minimizes the reflection coefficient magnitude while the matching-network elements remain fixed. The results show that frequency tuning strongly suppresses the reflected power during the pulse-on phase, while the power absorbed by the plasma changes only weakly under the imposed constant-generator-output-power condition. The results provide a proof-of-principle demonstration that driving-frequency modulation can compensate for transient impedance variations, reduce the reflected-power burden, and improve matching efficiency in pulsed CCPs without changing the matching-network elements within the pulse.
                  </jats:p>
title: Frequency-tuned impedance matching for pulsed capacitively coupled plasmas: analysis of self-consistent circuit-plasma coupling
